title: Cross-Border Ownership and Input Access: Evidence from the Lithium Supply Chain
abstract: arXiv:2611.08430v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How does cross-border ownership shape the lithium supply chain? Using global data on mines and refineries, I estimate a model in which ownership can lower refiners' effective ore costs, encourage mines to restrict spot sales, and soften competition. To study these effects, I examine policies motivated by national security concerns about reliable access to critical mineral inputs: divestiture of Chinese stakes in overseas producers and a ban on ore exports to China. Divestiture increases spot ore supply but leaves lithium output nearly unchanged, while continued trade preserves Chinese access to ore. The export ban reduces global lithium supply because refining capacity elsewhere cannot fully replace lost Chinese production. Ownership transfers do not reserve ore for domestic production; restricting Chinese access imposes a substantial supply cost at existing capacities.

translated_title: 跨境所有权与投入品获取：来自锂供应链的证据
translated_abstract: 跨境所有权如何塑造锂供应链？本文利用全球矿山和冶炼厂的全球数据，估计了一个模型，其中所有权可以降低冶炼厂的有效矿石成本、促使矿山限制现货销售，并弱化市场竞争。为研究这些效应，我考察了出于对关键矿物投入可靠获取的国家安全担忧而出台的两项政策：剥离中国在海外的生产企业的股份，以及禁止向中国出口矿石。研究结果表明，股权剥离增加了现货矿石供应，但锂产量几乎保持不变，而持续的贸易保持了中国获取矿石的渠道。出口禁令会减少全球锂供应，因为其他地区的冶炼产能无法完全替代中国损失的产量。所有权转移并不会将矿石保留给国内生产；在现有产能条件下，限制中国的矿石获取渠道会带来巨大的供应成本。
tldr: 本文利用全球锂矿与冶炼厂数据建立模型，发现剥离中国海外股权几乎不影响锂产量，而禁止矿石出口中国会显著减少全球锂供应，表明在现有产能下限制中国获取矿石的代价高昂。
en_tdlr: Using global data on lithium mines and refineries, this paper shows that divesting Chinese stakes leaves lithium output nearly unchanged, while banning ore exports to China substantially reduces global lithium supply, revealing the high cost of restricting Chinese access to critical mineral inputs.
